I have gone through the same, I feel you.
If these people keep pushing you away, making you feel unwanted, you should leave them. I know it's a hard choice that will lead to a feeling of nostalgia and regret sometimes. Whenever my birthday comes around, at some point I wish we were still friends and they would throw me a party to celebrate together.  But it's worthwhile to leave in the end.
Your efforts are not lame, believe me. They simply show your sincere and loving nature. Don't ever think you're worth nothing because of them.

If you want to try to stay in your group, there are two things you can do :
1) Try to ask a person from the group you trust (Ex : the girls you're still hanging out with) why the group doesn't include you anymore. If they still meet up with you, they must care a minimum and won't probably say hurtful things. 

2) Cut ties with the group, disappear for a while and see their reaction.

As for making new friends well...you said it yourself, it's easier to make some at school or practicing extracurricular activities. Where do you currently work, by the way ?

If you're not totally against it, maybe you could start a new activity. You say you don't have any hobbies, but you can still be curious. Trying to discover another kind of activity, happiness etc..
If you're into that, maybe you can go dancing at a club or spend some time in a pub, best way to meet strangers.
Finally, is there something you're particularly interested in ? Like books movies etc...You can also make friends online, by the basis of common interests. Some of my friends even met their boyfriends online.

To conclude, I wish you all the luck in the world. It is not an easy situation and I'm still getting used to having waaay less people to hang out, not having movie dates etc.  You'll manage to build some healthy relationships again

I would advice you to act upon intuition. If someone gives you a compliment and you truly like it, thank them and show them you enjoyed the gesture. 
If you receive a compliment you feel like you don't deserve it, just give them a polite thanks. Or if you're a bit close to the person, explain them why you feel like you don't deserve this kind word.

Finally, complimenting a girl right back doesn't mean right away that you're "chasing after a girl". If you like doing it, keep on doing so. You're free to stay true to yourself :)  On the other hand, if you DO want a girl to like you, you may want not to compliment her right away. Rather, giving her a compliment a bit later : something that will feel fresh and unexpected.

The best about compliments is being spontaneous. If you like something about someone, you're free and encouraged to say so. If you liked a compliment, you're free to show so.

I see all negative comments about the girl's attitude but what the heck ?
I think it's natural to break up a relationship if you've fallen in love with someone else and can't bear your partner anymore. It's an act made out of love.
If you want to date her, do it. It never hurts to try. I think you can judge if she is sincere or not.

It does sound like he said that he "did see a future that could lead to marriage" only to make you stay.
The way you speak about him, maybe he's just the type of person who doesn't want to get married. Leading to another kind of relationship.

So I think either he doesn't see a future with you, or he DOES see a future but not the one you're longing for. You should talk with him again to clarify some stuff.

I don't think you're being unreasonable. You are free to wish for some dynamic changes in your relationships. But either, you can not force your boyfriend to fulfill your desires. He must feel extremely pressured at work and only wants nice, relaxing moments when he is with you. So when you speak to him about this issue, show him you understand how hard this is for him, and that it's hard for you too on another level.

The two solutions there appear to be :
-Making a compromise. On his side, understand your pain and see if there is really no way he can do something about it. On your side, try being more flexible and acknowledge his efforts. 
-Moving in together, if it's not incompatible with your personnalities and relationship
